references.text: God repeats the warning to Moses about setting boundaries for the people so that they do not break through to see the Lord and many of them perish.
At the renewal of the covenant, God gives similar instructions that no one should go up on the mountain or be near it.
Moses reminds the people how they stood at the foot of the mountain burning with fire and describes the reverence required.
The book of Hebrews refers directly to this event and quotes the prohibition against touching the mountain, contrasting the Sinai covenant with the new covenant.
At the burning bush, Moses was told not to come closer because the place was holy, a similar principle about holiness and boundaries.
At the Jordan, the people had to keep their distance from the ark of the covenant, about two thousand cubits, and not come too near the holy thing.
Both verses illustrate the principle that access to the holy place is strictly regulated under threat of death for unauthorized persons.
Both verses define the boundaries of the holy space (the mountain/tent) where unauthorized proximity results in the death penalty.
The same historical event told in two books, showing that the principle of protecting the holy space (the king/mountain) with life is consistent.
